title: Bridging LLM Research -> Deployments: reading sprint notes
content:
Quick context: pulled together lightweight summaries from papers, posters, and follow-up blog posts during a short reading sprint — focused on things we can prototype in Redwood Dedicated/private within 2-3 sprints. Goal: identify low-risk experiments that have measurable latency/cost/quality tradeoffs and map to product levers (batching, KV caching, routing, quant profiles).

Top takeaways (high level):
- Sparse/conditional KV caches (paper A): major win for long-context cost if you can cheaply index/retrieve relevant KV subsets.
  - Key idea: learn a compact selector that routes a request to a small subset of KV shards instead of reading full cache.
  - Redwood implication: could reduce per-token memory bandwidth and RTX utilization for very long histories.
  - Quick experiment: prototype selector using approximate LSH on prefix embeddings; measure retrieval latency and hit-rate vs full-scan.
  - Metrics: average tokens/sec, p95 request latency, cache hit rate, effective token cost (GPU-seconds/token).

- Latent-prefix cache (poster B): store compressed representations upstream and reconstruct in model space when needed.
  - Idea: amortize recomputation by keeping small latent states that can be expanded to KV when used.
  - Redwood implication: trade memory for compute; useful for infrequent long-history requests.
  - Experiment: integrate simple autoencoder on prefix states in Dedicated staging pool; compare cold-start latency and memory footprint.

- Safety-oriented context trimming (paper C + sys blog): heuristics to remove toxic or PII-containing segments from long context before serving to reduce downstream risk and KV pollution.
  - Practical pattern: run a fast classifier on incoming context, tag and omit high-risk spans before cache insertion.
  - Redwood ops: add a pre-cache filter step in our routing pipeline; configurable per-customer policy.

Notes from ICLR 2026 lightning talks / posters:
- Several groups show >2x memory reduction with structured sparsity + quantization when combined with KV sparsification. Not magic; needs careful retraining/finetune.
- Papers repeatedly call out latency overhead of complex selectors — design for microsecond budgets if you want to maintain p95 SLAs.

Loose experiment plan (priority order):
1) LSH-based KV selector (2-week spike)
   - Deliverable: bench that compares full-scan vs LSH-selection on synthetic prefix sets (10k sessions).
   - Success criteria: >=30% reduction in average memory read bandwidth and <=5% degradation in downstream generation quality (BLEU/ROUGE or human quick sweep).
   - Owners: Owen (selector proto), me (eval harness), Sofia (runtime hook).

2) Pre-cache safety filter (1 sprint)
   - Deliverable: policy-prototype and opt-in customer config in staging.
   - Success criteria: catch >90% of seeded PII/toxicity spans with <1% false positive on clean dialogues.

3) Latent-prefix micro-proto (2 sprints)
   - Deliverable: tiny autoencoder + integration to backup expansion path when prefix requested.
   - Success criteria: memory reduction >20% on long sessions and cold expansion latency <200ms for p50.

Open questions / risks:
- Selector false negatives: if selector misses critical KV entries, hallucination risk increases. Need small human eval set for safety-critical prompts.
- Index maintenance: how often do we rebuild LSH indexes? Real-time insert/delete costs matter for Dedicated streaming.
- Instrumentation: need token-level tracing to attribute errors to cache misses vs model drift. Add tags in tracing pipeline.

Meeting prep (sync with serving-runtime + SRE):
- Quick agenda: demo proto plan, resource estimate (GPU h/w + memory), SLO impact, rollout gating (canary on Dedicated only).
- Ask SRE: what metrics are easiest to surface in Console for per-route cache-hit vs token-cost?

Tiny notes / heuristics to remember:
- Always measure cost in both tokens and GPU-seconds (sometimes cache saves tokens but adds GPU work).
- Keep canary fallback simple: if selector latency > threshold, fall back to full-scan variant.

Immediate TODOs (next 72h):
- Owen: spin up LSH spike dataset and share README. (JIRA-OPS-1147)
- Me: draft eval harness (small human-label set) and post to Confluence link above.
- Sofia: check PR #523 for runtime extension points and list required hooks.

Random links/readings I flagged: 
- "Efficient KV routing for long-context LMs" (paper A) — arXiv 2026 (notes in confluence)
- "Latent Prefixes: Compressed histories" (poster B) — ICLR 2026 slides
- "Context trimming for safety" blog post — companyX blog, July 2026

Notes-to-self: keep this doc terse; convert into proper RFC if spike shows promise. When writing RFC, include regression evaluation with our standard prompt-suite and embed per-route cost plots (tokens, GPU time, p95 latency).

End scribbles — will update after first spike results.
